title: Multiple Effect Evaporator

introduction.definition: A multiple effect evaporator uses the vapour produced in one effect as the heating steam for the next, which works at a lower pressure so its liquid boils at a lower temperature. Only the first effect takes live steam, so each kilogram of steam evaporates several kilograms of water.
key_points: Steam economy ≈ N × (0.8–1) for N effects
Pressure and boiling point fall from effect to effect
Total ΔT is shared between effects → more area
Forward, backward or mixed feed arrangements
introduction.summary: A multiple effect evaporator uses the vapour from one evaporator body (effect) as the heating steam of the next, which runs at lower pressure and boiling point. Only the first effect uses live steam, so steam consumption per kilogram of water evaporated falls roughly in proportion to the number of effects.

pressure.title: Pressure and boiling point fall from effect to effect
pressure.description: Effect 1 operates at the highest pressure and temperature, heated by live steam. Its vapour is hot enough to boil the liquor in effect 2, which runs at a lower pressure (lower boiling point), and so on to the last effect under vacuum. Each kilogram of steam evaporates roughly N × 0.8–1 kg of water in N effects (steam economy), at the cost of more heating surface.

foundation: Support vessels on structure/legs designed for operating and flooded weights; allow thermal growth of calandrias and vapour lines.
alignment: Vertical calandrias plumb (falling-film distribution depends on it); slope liquor lines for drainage.
piping: Vapour lines sized for low ΔP; condensate drained by traps or level control; vents for non-condensables on each steam chest.
Vacuum system (condenser + vacuum pump/ejector) for the last effect.
commissioning: Leak/vacuum test; water trials (wetting, levels); bring steam on slowly; set levels and densities; CIP routine.

routine.task: Monitor pressures, levels and densities of each effect.

periodic.task: Clean effects in rotation; check vacuum system.

lubrication: No lubrication for the static parts — lubricate valve stems, rotating parts and drives per maker.

safety: Vacuum and pressure ratings; hot liquor; isolate steam before entry.

video_tutorials.title: Multiple Effect Evaporator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Multiple Effect Evaporator.
A multiple effect evaporator uses the vapour produced in one effect as the heating steam for the next, which works at a lower pressure so its liquid boils at a lower temperature.
Only the first effect takes live steam, so each kilogram of steam evaporates several kilograms of water.
Typical applications include sugar, pulp & paper (black liquor), dairy; caustic soda and chemical concentration; desalination (MED).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Effect 1: Calandria (steam chest), Effect 2: Calandria (steam chest), Effect 3: Calandria (steam chest).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Multiple Effect Evaporator — Operation

script.narration: How the Multiple Effect Evaporator works.
Live steam heats effect 1.
Vapour from effect 1 heats effect 2 at lower pressure.
Effect 3 works under vacuum, heated by effect 2 vapour.
Liquor flows forward from effect to effect.
The last vapour is condensed in the condenser.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Effect 1 operates at the highest pressure and temperature, heated by live steam.

video_tutorials.title: Multiple Effect Evaporator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Multiple Effect Evaporator.
Monitor pressures, levels and densities of each effect.
Clean effects in rotation; check vacuum system.
Inspect tubes and vapour lines.
Watch for loss of vacuum: falling capacity, rising last-effect temperature. Common cause: air leaks, condenser fouling.
Watch for scaling in later effects: falling ΔT, capacity. Common cause: concentration and solubility.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
